request.brief: I am building a cybersecurity product.

surfaces.value: A marketing site and probably a product interface

signals.range: Body text at 7:1 or above on the main ground
signals.because: Security tools tend to involve dense tables and logs. This is inferred from the offering.

signals.range: One direction stays quiet, one departs from category colors, one reworks the dark theme
signals.because: The brief does not say whether to fit in with competitors or stand apart.
Nothing in the brief favors one.

directions.name: Audit Trail
directions.summary: Cool grays and a precise ink, with amber reserved for what needs attention.

secondary.evidence: 100% of chroma-weighted area lies in the cool arc.

method.chroma: Holds relative chroma from the base, capped at 1.1 times the base C.
Holds relative chroma from the base, capped at 1.1 times the base C.
Holds the base C, capped below the sRGB limit at each L.

reasoning.claim: Body Ink reaches 13.82:1 on Report White, which suits dense tables and logs read for long periods.
Chromatic color is limited to 4% of the declared area, so amber keeps its value as a signal.
A quiet interface lets alerts and data carry the urgency, which suits teams who spend all day in the product.

do: Keep the interface achromatic and let data carry the color.
Reserve Flag Amber for items that need a decision.
avoid: Do not use Flag Amber decoratively.
Do not rely on amber alone to communicate severity.

accessibility.standard: WCAG 2.2 contrast computed from sRGB HEX
notes: Contrast applies to the listed pairs only. Check any new pairing before use.
Do not rely on color alone for meaning. Pair state or status color with text, shape or an icon (WCAG 1.4.1).
Flag Amber and Slate are specified for components, not body text.

directions.name: Clear Signal
directions.summary: A bright persimmon on warm white, deliberately away from the usual blue or neon green.

secondary.evidence: 79% of chroma-weighted area lies in the warm arc.
Persimmon and Teal Check differ by 152 degrees.

method.chroma: Holds relative chroma from the base, capped at 1.1 times the base C.
Holds relative chroma from the base, capped at 1.1 times the base C.
Holds the base C, capped below the sRGB limit at each L.

reasoning.claim: Aubergine reaches 13.04:1 on Warm White, so it can carry headings and dark sections while Persimmon remains the identity color.
Blue interfaces and neon on black are common in this category, so a warm lead color is a deliberate way to differ. Confirm against the actual competitors.
Persimmon reaches 4.29:1 on Warm White, so it is specified for large type and components.

do: Use Persimmon for the brand mark, large headlines and illustration.
Use Aubergine for dark sections and navigation.
avoid: Do not use Persimmon for error states, because it could be confused with the brand color.

accessibility.standard: WCAG 2.2 contrast computed from sRGB HEX
notes: Contrast applies to the listed pairs only. Check any new pairing before use.
Do not rely on color alone for meaning. Pair state or status color with text, shape or an icon (WCAG 1.4.1).
A product interface would need separate status colors, which this direction does not define.

directions.name: Night Shift
directions.summary: A dark violet-gray ground with one electric chartreuse and a periwinkle support.

secondary.evidence: 65% of chroma-weighted area lies in the cool arc.
Chartreuse and Periwinkle differ by 166 degrees.
Primary reaches 13.5:1 on the foundation and 100% of figure area reaches 4.5:1.

method.chroma: Holds relative chroma from the base, capped at 1.1 times the base C.
Holds relative chroma from the base, capped at 1.1 times the base C.
Holds the base C, capped below the sRGB limit at each L.

reasoning.claim: Chartreuse reaches 13.5:1 on Night Violet, so a small amount carries a lot of emphasis.
A tinted violet-gray ground gives a dark theme more character than the common blue-black.
Cool Paper carries body text at 14.86:1, so reading does not depend on the saturated colors.

do: Use Chartreuse sparingly for the primary action and key data.
Use Periwinkle for links and secondary emphasis.
avoid: Do not fill large areas with Chartreuse.
Do not add glows or neon gradients.

accessibility.standard: WCAG 2.2 contrast computed from sRGB HEX
notes: Contrast applies to the listed pairs only. Check any new pairing before use.
Do not rely on color alone for meaning. Pair state or status color with text, shape or an icon (WCAG 1.4.1).

openQuestions: Is the buyer a security team, an IT generalist or a consumer?
Does the product need both light and dark themes?
What do the direct competitors use?
Which status colors does the product need?
